text:
sam: Heads up — helm upgrade of gpu-allocator chart to v2.2 in us-west-2 started but hit a post-upgrade hook problem. Post-hook deployed a mutating webhook that immediately started rejecting pod admits: 'admission webhook \"gpu-alloc.redwood.ai\" denied: unknown label'. Seeing a bunch of pods stuck Pending and some long-running jobs evicted. Cluster autoscaler then removed two GPU nodes and capacity dropped.
deploy-bot: release pipeline #4578 failed at step post-upgrade-hook. Logs: 
  2026-03-18T14:02:11Z helm: post-upgrade hook create mutatingwebhookconfiguration/gpu-alloc succeeded
  2026-03-18T14:03:05Z controller: admission failures spike

liz: ouch. Any quick mitigation? if we can flip failurePolicy to Ignore that should stop new rejects while we investigate the webhook logic.
tim: also worth scaling the gpu nodepool up temporarily so we don't lose running jobs. autoscaler removed nodes because a bunch of pods were unschedulable. Might be terraform/nodepool label drift — I've seen labels missing for the new provisioning tag.

alex: tried helm rollback but got: 'error: release gpu-allocator failed: timed out waiting for the condition; hook delete failed: resource is already terminating' — looks like the hook resources are stuck Terminating (webhook config + job). Also a PVC finalizer showed up blocking pre-delete cleanup for some dataset mounts.

maria: quick triage notes — chart v2.2 introduces a CRD schema bump (GpuAllocation v1beta1 -> v1). The new webhook validates label keys that older controllers don't add yet, so mismatch. Short-term: patch the mutatingwebhookconfiguration to set failurePolicy: Ignore and remove the specific label validation rule. Longer-term: coordinate controller rollout with CRD conversion.

sam: can someone paste the kubectl patch command? I can run it in us-west-2.

maria: run this to set ignore on the webhook (namespace/global resource):

kubectl patch mutatingwebhookconfiguration gpu-alloc -p '[{"op":"replace","path":"/webhooks/0/failurePolicy","value":"Ignore"}]' --type=json

That will stop new rejects; it doesn't fix already Pending pods though.
tim: scaling nodepool now: gcloud container clusters update redwood-usw2 --update-addons=NodeLocalDNS --region=us-west2 && gcloud container node-pools resize gpu-pool --cluster=redwood-usw2 --region=us-west2 --num-nodes=5

ops-bot: Node-pool scale request submitted to cloud provider (request id: r-7f2a). ETA ~3m.

alex: after setting failurePolicy=Ignore I attempted a helm rollback with --force; rollback proceeds but the pre-delete hook still hangs on PVC finalizer. There's a couple of dataset PVCs with protection.finalizers.kubernetes.io present. We might need to remove that finalizer manually to allow cleanup.

liz: please don't remove finalizers blindly — confirm no running job mounts them. If we must, delete finalizer only on the specific PVCs that show 'Terminating' for >15m and whose pods are defunct.

maria: also opened a quick terraform drift check on nodepool labels — if terraform removed gpu-type label during a previous upgrade, autoscaler decisions could be wrong. Throwing the drift report link: https://infra-reports.internal/terraform-drift/gpu-pools/us-west-2

sam: I'm applying the webhook patch now and scaling nodes. After ops-bot confirms nodes, we'll triage PVC finalizers carefully. If rollback is still blocked we'll coordinate a controlled force-delete of the stuck hook resources and reapply the previous chart version.

ops-bot: webhook patch applied by sam at 2026-03-18T14:12:03Z. Node-pool scaled to 5 nodes at 2026-03-18T14:15:20Z.

tim: nodes are up, pods are getting scheduled again, admission errors dropped to near-zero in the last 2m. Starting to drain and re-create any pods stuck in CrashLoop.

alex: I'm going through PVCs now — three PVCs had finalizers. Two were safe to remove (no active pods). Removed finalizers and pre-delete hooks cleaned up. Helm rollback succeeded with --force at 2026-03-18T14:31:10Z.

sam: thanks team. Action items: 1) revert chart to v2.1 until we coordinate CRD migration + controller rollout, 2) add a preflight validation step in release pipeline that checks CRD/controller compatibility, 3) add a docs note about failurePolicy defaults for mutating webhooks during rollout. I'll open follow-ups in eng-releases and infra.

liz: +1 — also let's add a non-blocking canary for webhook schema checks in CI to catch this earlier.

ops-bot: follow-up ticket created: INFRA-9941 'gpu-allocator post-upgrade webhook caused admission rejects; add preflight + CRD migration plan' assigned to sam.

maria: good postmortem note: this was a classic controller/CRD/version skew during a multi-component chart upgrade. Avoid in future by decoupling CRD changes from webhook/logic changes (two-step rollout).
